preamble: Prothesis of [w] before an initial rounded back vowel is best documented in English: from the 14th century, south-western and western dialects began to pronounce Old English ān 'one' with an initial /w/, a form that became standard by the 18th century (compare dialectal woak 'oak').

examples.from: Middle English on / one 'one' (< Old English ān)
examples.note: The /w/ arose in south-western and western England around the 14th century and was standard by the 18th; alone, atone and only keep the older form, and once shows the same /w/.
The same prothesis in a dialect form cited as a parallel to one.

sources: Wiktionary contributors. one (English pronunciation history). https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/one
